title: finding(devx): `check-lint-rule-coverage` walks gitignored build output, so the gate turns red after any local build (`apps/console/plugin.js`)
body:
Filed unassigned by the `domain:devx` execution seat while implementing objectui#7995. Recording, not claiming — nothing in that card touches this gate.

## What happens

`check:lint-rule-coverage` (`scripts/check-lint-rule-coverage.mjs`) walks files that git ignores. `apps/console/plugin.js` is a build OUTPUT — `apps/console/.gitignore:16` names it, and it is absent from `HEAD` — and after a local `turbo run build` the gate reports it as an `unledgered` zero-rule file and exits 1.

Measured on `411a132c0` plus the objectui#7995 branch (a two-file `scripts/` diff that cannot reach `apps/console`):

```
before any build      pnpm check:lint-rule-coverage   exit 0
after turbo run build pnpm check:lint-rule-coverage   exit 1
                        unledgered: apps/console/plugin.js
                        census: 4450 walked, 4325 rule-bearing, 125 zero-rule
control: rm apps/console/plugin.js, re-run          exit 0
```

The pin fails with it: `scripts/__tests__/check-lint-rule-coverage.test.ts` "is green, with every ledger row still live and the census standing" asserts `result.findings` deeply equals the empty array, and it goes red on the same single entry. Removing the artifact turns both green again, with no other change to the tree — so the artifact is the whole cause.

## Why it is worth recording

The failure mode is the one a coverage gate can least afford: **the verdict depends on whether the developer happened to build**, and it points at a file nobody wrote and nobody can fix at the site. The two available "repairs" are both wrong — adding a `VACUOUS_GROUPS` row for a generated file puts a permanent ledger entry against a path that is not in the repository, and adding rules in `eslint.config.js` for build output is worse.

It also fails in the direction that costs a whole round: an agent who builds locally (which several of the doc gates REQUIRE — `check:doc-snippets`, `check:doc-examples` and `check:skill-examples` all exit 2 with "run the build first") then reads a red `check:lint-rule-coverage` as damage from their own diff, and goes looking for it in `scripts/`.

## Not a duplicate

objectui#8337 is the nearest neighbour and it is the other half of the same surface question: it records files ESLint does NOT walk (`.mts`/`.cts`). This one records a file it DOES walk and should not. Dedup was a REST listing of all 453 open issues plus a local grep; the control term `spec-symbol-derivation` returned its two known cards, so the empty result for `lint-rule-coverage` is a real read rather than a silent failure.

## Shape, not a ruling

The census walk presumably needs to ask git whether a path is ignored (`git check-ignore`, or enumerate from `git ls-files` instead of the filesystem) before counting it. Whether the answer belongs in the walk or in a declared exclusion is the queue call, not this card.
